title: hybrid-kernel-profiles-and-kv-snapshot-scheduler-for-irregular-heads
author: Anika Shah
description:
Motivation: Several customers reported higher-than-expected tail latency and throughput variance on models that mix head geometries (e.g. Qwen grouped heads, Mistral aggregated blocks, and certain Llama forks that pack attention heads unevenly). Root cause: the existing single-profile kernel selection + simple kv prefetching is brittle when the runtime sees sudden changes in effective head stride and sequence length distribution during continuous batching. This PR introduces two coordinated runtime improvements: 1) hybrid kernel profiles - a compact per-model policy that enumerates candidate kernel families (NV/Planar/Interleaved) with quick heuristics for head/seq shapes and an adaptive fallback ordering; 2) KV snapshot scheduler - a lightweight snapshot-and-replay mechanism that captures a short-lived KV layout and pre-warms per-shard KV pages for the dominant kernel choice before executing the full batch. Together these reduce misaligned kernel fallbacks and reduce cold-KV penalties during dynamic batching.

What changed (summary): commits add a kernel_profile JSON schema and parser, a new HybridKernelSelector component, a KVSnapshotScheduler that integrates with continuous-batching, unit and perf tests, and ops documentation. We added a small telemetry flag (runtime.experimental.hybrid_profiles) gated off by default and enabled for the internal perf stage. Work items: ENG-8742 (design), ENG-8799 (implementation), SUP-4421 (customer incident triage).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and perf plan (linked in Linear) - [x] Kernel selector + profile schema implemented - [x] KV snapshot scheduler implemented and integrated with batcher - [x] Unit tests added for selector heuristics - [x] Perf harness and end-to-end microbench - [x] Docs for ops + rollout notes - [x] Feature gated and toggle added

Commits (high level): - 7f4c2b2: Add kernel_profile schema + parser + tests - a8bbd11: Implement HybridKernelSelector with heuristics for head-stride, group-count and seq-range - 3c9d2e6: KVSnapshotScheduler and integration hooks with BatchRunner - 9d3a1f0: Perf bench harness changes and new CI perf job - b21f8a4: Docs and rollout guide - 2b7c4a1: Fix: race in KV snapshot replay (addressed reviewer comment)

Files changed (high level): - src/runtime/kernel_profiles.cc / .h - src/runtime/hybrid_kernel_selector.cc / .h - src/runtime/kv_snapshot_scheduler.cc / .h - src/runtime/batching/batch_runner.cc (integration hooks) - tests/unit/test_kernel_profiles.cpp - tests/perf/kv_snapshot_bench.py - docs/ops/kernel-profiles.md - scripts/bench/run_kv_snapshots.sh - tools/telemetry/flags.yaml

Notable implementation details: - HybridKernelSelector: keeps a tiny LRU cache of (model_version, head_config)->preferred_kernel_family and fallbacks with recent success counts. Selection heuristics include head_stride parity, group_count ratio, and observed token latency trend. The cache is sharded per-worker to avoid global contention. - KVSnapshotScheduler: when a batch is assembled we compute a short-lived "snapshot key" (model_version + kernel_family_hint + leading sequence histogram). Scheduler may prefetch KV pages for shards corresponding to the snapshot and attach a small prioritized replay step to warm per-GPU allocator metadata. The snapshot window is tunable (default 16 batches). - Safety: snapshots are advisory; if prefetch fails or detects mismatch we fall back to the existing prefetch path. We added time-budget checks to avoid violating P99 latency SLOs. - Telemetry: added runtime counters for snapshot hits/misses, kernel switch count, fallback events, and per-model snapshot stall time. These are sparse by default.

Benchmarks: microbench on c6g.xlarge-gpu clusters (mixed Mistral-8/llama-70b-q4 models): - Mistral-8: P95 latency down 9.3% with hybrid profiles + snapshots (default batching, seq=512) - Llama-70b-q4: tokens/sec +6.8% under continuous batching with mixed sequence lengths - Qwen-grouped: P99 latency reduced 11% on synthetic head-stride jitter tests - End-to-end e2e test (customer workload repro): 8% lower cost per token for sustained 30-minute runs. Notes: improvements larger for workloads with head-geometry churn; near-zero regression for stable, homogeneous workloads.

Rollout plan / Ops notes: - Feature gated: runtime.experimental.hybrid_profiles=false by default. Ops can enable per-cluster with config flag. - Phase 1: enable on internal perf cluster for 72h with telemetry; Phase 2: A/B 10% of traffic for customers with known head-geometry variance; Phase 3: wide rollout if no regressions. - Quick rollback: toggle off the feature; KVSnapshotScheduler is non-blocking if disabled. - Watch metrics: snapshot_hit_rate, kernel_switch_rate, per-model p95 latency.

Review conversation (abridged): Miguel Ortega (review): "Nice design. Two concerns: 1) shards could be warmed unnecessarily if snapshot heuristics are too eager; 2) how does this interact with multi-tenant dedicated pools?" Anika Shah (author): "Added snapshot budget checks (max_prefetch_pages per-GPU) and per-tenant quota in the scheduler; non-default gate avoids surprise in Dedicated. See kv_snapshot_scheduler.cc lines ~210-280 for budget logic." Priya Raman (review): "Can we tighten the heuristic for Qwen grouped heads? I recommend adding group-aware stride check." Anika: "Added group_count ratio check and unit tests around the Qwen pattern (test_kernel_profiles.cpp)." Evan Liu (review): "CI failed on perf; please add perf cold-run stability test." Anika: "Added kv_snapshot_bench.py and a CI perf job; re-ran and green." Final approval comments: Miguel "LGTM, small nits addressed"; Priya "Approved"; Evan "Approved".

CI summary: Initial run (main job matrix) reported a perf job failure due to flaky cold-start timing (investigated and reproduced in perf harness). After adding a short stabilization sleep in the bench harness and tightening timeouts, CI passed. Full CI: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, perf: pass (stabilized), lint: pass. Telemetry smoke job: pass.

Compatibility & breaking changes: non-breaking. The kernel profile parser will ignore unknown fields. The KVSnapshotScheduler introduces telemetry and knobs but is off by default.

Release notes: "Introduce hybrid kernel profiles and a KV snapshot scheduler to reduce kernel fallback and cold-KV penalties for models with irregular head geometries (opt-in experimental feature)."

Merge: merged via squash-merge. Merge commit: "squash! hybrid: hybrid kernel profiles + kv snapshot scheduler (ENG-8742, ENG-8799)".

Follow-ups: - ENG-8851: add adaptive snapshot window based on live latency signals - ENG-8864: expose per-model tuning UI in Console - ENG-8899: integrate with Dedicated autoscaler policies to avoid unnecessary prefetch on constrained pools
